panels.title: Published nodes
panels.description: Nodes on /stable.txt after the last PUBLISHED cycle - the list a client actually receives. A cycle that fails leaves the previous value standing, so read it against 'Publish age': a healthy number with a stale age is last hour's list.

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: Sources that returned a usable body against sources configured, published once per cycle, so both trail a config edit by a cycle and ok below total means fetch failures that cycle. Instant read: with nothing exported right now the tile shows neutral No data, which is also every restart before the first published cycle.

panels.title: Publish age
panels.description: Seconds since the last cycle that PUBLISHED a list, rendered as an age: a cycle that runs and fails does not reset it, so this is how stale the list is, not when the worker last ran. Read as an instant query — nothing exported now reads No data whatever the time range, and cannot tell a restart from a dead scrape.

panels.title: Pipeline funnel
panels.description: Last cycle counted through the pipeline, in legend order: merged (unique nodes after dedupe), probed, dead-skipped (never probed — a recent probe found them dead), kept (published). merged = dead-skipped + probed, so the merged-to-probed gap is the dead cache, not loss; probed to kept is the probe plus the gates.

panels.title: Cycle health
panels.description: Wall time of the last published cycle in seconds on the left axis; cycles and failures counted over a rolling hour on the right. cycles/h counts every attempt, published or failed, so failures/h is a subset of it — and both counters are exported before the first cycle publishes, when duration is still absent.

panels.title: IP-stage yield
panels.description: Nodes every source yielded against those that survived the IP stage, survival share on the right axis. Both are summed per source before dedupe, so survived normally sits far above merged, equal only when nothing is left to dedupe. "fetched" excludes lines the parser refused, counted as reason=unsupported.

panels.title: IP-stage drops
panels.description: Nodes the per-node IP-stage filters dropped in preprocess, summed over every source and split by reason. unsupported is not a filter drop — it counts unparseable input lines, which never entered the fetched total — and a flat zero on geo, asn or cidr may mean the selected job's instance configures no such filter. Legend values are the last non-null samples in the selected range; a stopped series can retain its last value here. A gap is not zero.

panels.title: Feeds: top 25

targets.expr: sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_nodes_total{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))
sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_tested_nodes{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))
sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_published_nodes{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))

panels.description: Top 25 (feed, owner) pairs ranked by IP passed in the last published cycle. Counts sum the sources in each pair. A feed is the recorded channel, or the source name when none is recorded; owner is crawler or curated. Fetched / IP passed / Probe passed / Published map to nodes_total / valid_nodes / tested_nodes / published_nodes. Names are unchanged. IP passed is pre-merge and can count shared nodes more than once; Published is attribution after deduplication.

panels.title: Source ownership
panels.description: Last published cycle, summed by owner (crawler or curated) and sorted by IP passed. sources counts sources that reported, not all configured sources. Fetched / IP passed / Probe passed / Published map to nodes_total / valid_nodes / tested_nodes / published_nodes. Published is attribution, not contribution: curated sources merge first and claim shared nodes.

panels.title: Crawler sources
panels.description: Top 25 crawler-managed sources ranked by IP passed in the last published cycle; source identifiers are unchanged. Fetched / IP passed / Probe passed / Published map to nodes_total / valid_nodes / tested_nodes / published_nodes. IP passed is pre-merge; deduplication, dead-cache skips and probe failures all reduce Probe passed. Do not compare rows directly with curated sources, which claim shared nodes first.

panels.title: Curated sources
panels.description: Top 25 hand-curated sources ranked by IP passed in the last published cycle; source identifiers are unchanged. Fetched / IP passed / Probe passed / Published map to nodes_total / valid_nodes / tested_nodes / published_nodes. Curated sources merge first and claim shared nodes, so Probe passed and Published are attribution, not a direct quality comparison with crawler sources.

panels.title: TCP reachability
panels.description: What the probe phase's TCP reachability pre-check did, in distinct server:port endpoints — never the condemned NODE count on the probe-outcome panel. trusted = 1: refused endpoints were condemned unprobed and dead-cached; trusted = 0: the breaker rejected the verdict and every node was probed; unresolved fails open.

panels.title: Probe outcomes
panels.description: Where the probe ended for each node probed, stacked to close over probed: condemned (the TCP pre-check refused the server, no URL test spent), connect, fetch, passed, unknown (no result at all — its mapping did not parse and its endpoint was never condemned). A condemned node is also dead-cached for hours, so it leaves the next few cycles' probed count.

panels.title: Probe refusals
panels.description: Probed nodes no URL test could be built for, split by who refused them: unconvertible = the share-link converter emitted no mapping for the scheme, unparsable = it did and mihomo refused the mapping. With stable_probe_outcome_nodes these partition stable_probed_nodes, so a gap between the two panels and "probed" is a prober without the refusal account.

panels.title: Cycle time by phase
panels.description: Stacked per-phase wall time, in seconds, of the last cycle that PUBLISHED — an aborted cycle leaves the previous one standing. The unstacked total runs above the stack because the steps between phases belong to no phase, and probe covers the whole Probe call including the TCP pre-check, which has no phase of its own.

panels.title: Filter coverage
panels.description: Nodes entering, leaving and actually classified by each through-node gate, in chain order: every gate's 'in' is the previous gate's 'kept', so the ladder is the egress funnel. 'verified' counts entries whose check reached a conclusive verdict - a clean pass or a refusal - and 'unverified' those that answered without the evidence the classifier reads; both count entry labels of the last published cycle. An entry that never answered appears in neither: a believed batch drops it as unreachable, while a tripped batch keeps it and zeroes that drop (verdict trusted 0 on the panel beside this one). A gate that ran and verified nothing draws verified 0 rather than disappearing, while a gate that never ran - or the bandwidth filter, which has no API verdict account - draws no coverage line. stable_filter_trusted on the panel beside this one separates a believed drop policy from a tripped breaker. Each filter's in/kept pair shares one fixed color: dashed in, solid kept. This color pairing does not apply to verified/unverified lines. Legend values are the last non-null samples in the selected range, not necessarily current values.

panels.title: Filter drops & trust
panels.description: Nodes each through-node gate dropped, by reason: blocked (service answered, refused this egress), unreachable (never completed through the node), slow (under the bandwidth minimum). A zero line means the gate ran and dropped nobody — but not necessarily a clean pass: a gate whose whole survivor batch was condemned had the verdict disbelieved by the plausibility breaker, kept every survivor, and booked the same present zeros, warning instead. Each gate's "verdict trusted" line (stable_filter_trusted, right axis) tells the two apart: 1 = the verdict was believed and its drops were enacted last cycle, 0 = the breaker rejected it and nothing was dropped, no line = the gate reached no verdict — unconfigured, no usable key, or cancelled. Legend values are the last non-null samples in the selected range; a stopped series can retain its last value here. A gap is not zero.

panels.title: Cloudflare trace
panels.description: Published nodes split by whether Cloudflare's cdn-cgi/trace answered, plus moved — answered nodes whose measured egress country differs from the one the offline chain assigned. Nothing here drops a node, and moved is counted over answered nodes only, so a large unanswered share makes it less representative. Legend values are the last non-null samples in the selected range; a stopped series can retain its last value here. A gap is not zero.

panels.title: Kept-node speed
panels.description: Download speed of the nodes published last cycle: exact avg and max, plus p50/p90 interpolated from fixed buckets topping out at 500 Mbps, so a quantile pinned at 500 means faster than 500, not a plateau. With no bandwidth filter configured, avg still draws a flat zero while p50/p90 and max vanish.

panels.title: Kept-node latency
panels.description: Mean per-node probe delay in ms over the nodes published last cycle — the value the survivor gate (check.max_avg_ms) admits on and then sorts the list by. Read p90 and max against this job's own threshold: well under it the gate is not binding, pressed against it the cut is sitting inside the live population.

panels.title: Minimum speed
panels.description: Slowest kept node's measured download speed last cycle: the floor of the speed histogram panel, and the answer to whether the bandwidth gate is cutting inside the live population. Exported only when a cycle measured at least one kept-node speed, so No data means nothing was measured that cycle, exactly like the max line on the speed panel.

panels.title: Minimum latency
panels.description: Fastest kept node's mean probe delay last cycle: the head of the latency histogram panel, shown on its own tile because the histogram panel plots the max and the quantiles. Every kept survivor carries a latency, so No data here means no cycle has published nodes yet, not a missing measurement.

panels.title: Published countries
panels.description: Node counts per country over the published list only, top 15 of the last cycle. topk returns a bar solely for countries that have nodes, so a collapsed cycle shows fewer; bar colour is scaled to the largest bar, encoding share of the top country rather than health, and unplaceable nodes are absent from this metric.

panels.title: Unresolved GEO tags
panels.description: Published nodes whose GEO tag came out [GEO:??] because no annotation provider resolved a country, as a count on the left axis and a percentage of the published list on the right. These nodes are absent from the per-country metric, so a collapsing annotation chain is visible only here.

panels.title: Telegram topic funnel
panels.description: Forum-topic windows the crawler read per hour and what they yielded: pages fetched, pages carrying a live subscription URL, and new chats discovered from them. live/pages is the seed list's precision; discovered is the frontier it opens.

panels.title: Telegram empty reads
panels.description: Reads that returned nothing per hour: topic windows with no message (topic_empty) and bare groups whose /s listing carries no message wrap (group_empty). Both are pure cost - a group_empty rate climbing with no discovery means the frontier is filling with bare group refs.

panels.title: GitHub candidates
panels.description: Candidate files the GitHub discovery phase fetched per hour, in legend order: probed (bodies fetched), live (carried nodes), accepted (cleared the novelty floor and reached the mint). live/probed is candidate-filter precision and accepted/live the marginal gate's cut — a probed line climbing while live sits flat means the candidate scoring admits junk.

panels.title: GitHub new endpoints
panels.description: Distinct endpoints the accepted files added beyond the census, per hour — the phase's yield. Read against accepted on the funnel panel: novel/accepted is the mean novelty per accepted file, and a yield pinned near zero while probed keeps climbing means the corpus already carries what GitHub publishes or the novelty floor sits above it.

panels.title: GitHub search funnel
panels.description: Searches the GitHub phase spent per hour and what they admitted: repos (admitted and treed) and skipped (refused by the freshness/archived/fork gates before any tree call). repos/(repos+skipped) is the admission share of the searched population — a skipped-heavy pair means the queries surface stale or archived repositories, and searches climbing while repos stay flat means the cycle is spending its search budget on repositories the gates then refuse.

panels.title: GitHub limits & errors
panels.description: Rate-limit sleeps and every failure inside the GitHub phase, per hour. A sleeps line climbing means the per-cycle search caps sit above the token's limits - lower GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE/GITHUB_SEARCH_REPO. The errors line counts API, transport AND per-candidate probe failures, so read it as a rate: a low steady one is candidate churn (a file that vanished between the tree listing and the fetch), a step change is the token, the network or a GitHub outage.

panels.title: GitHub withdrawals
panels.description: GitHub-minted sources probation withdrew per hour: dropped from private.yaml and dead-stamped after GITHUB_PROBATION consecutive survivor-free service cycles. A rise means sources minted on novelty that the probe never validated are leaving the corpus; a rise to the size of the intake means the phase is paying nothing.
